topic: bro-harness dispatched-agent ergonomics: apply_patch tool + nudge note-compulsion
notes:
Consolidated from dogfood threads thread-c38e005d (notes 13/14) + thread-b797e515 (now retired). Citations VALIDATED against beta/blackbox-v2 (9cb5228). These are bro-harness tool/hook surface issues, independent of the cockpit + daemon arch.

B1 [OPEN] No apply_patch tool. crates/bro-tools/src/lib.rs:39-62 builtin_tools() ships FileRead/SmartRead/FileEdit/FileWrite/ListDir/ContentSearch/Glob/Shell*/Git*/WebFetch/TodoWrite/Sandbox*/EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree — no apply_patch. Dispatched agents repeatedly fall back to FileEdit (exact-match strict-refuse), and anchor-fail is recurring friction. Reference impl: ~/repos/codex/ ; the repo already has lark grammar cutpoints reusable for parsing the patch envelope (per thread-c38e005d note 13). Fix shape: add an apply_patch Tool that takes a unified/codex-style patch envelope, applies with fuzz, reports per-hunk results.

B2 [OPEN] Nudge GAP_NOTE_DIRECTIVE compulsion — no dedup/rate-limit + no orchestrator suppression. crates/bro-harness/src/hooks.rs:38-42 defines GAP_NOTE_DIRECTIVE; HookEngine::admit appends it unconditionally to every FIRED nudge (hooks.rs:242, `format!("{}{GAP_NOTE_DIRECTIVE}", c.message)`). It's gated by the ledger (signpost once/session, periodic respects cooldown) so not literally every turn, but under sustained tool friction a nudge-per-failed-call compels a bbox_note(kind=followup) each time → one driver produced ~40 near-identical notes in ~25 min, and an orchestrator "stop emitting notes" is UNSATISFIABLE against the harness directive (doom-loop). Tracked as gap-00659006 (HIGH). Fix shape: dedup/coalesce by (tool, gap-class) per session; a dispatch-level flag / orchestrator signal that quiets or down-weights the directive so "quiet down" is satisfiable.

Note: B2 pairs naturally with the daemon-side note-write cost (gap-a4e13310, see thread-935b467d A3) — a note-storm is doubly expensive when each resolve rewrites the whole store.

B3 [OPEN, VALIDATED from live transcript] bro-tools `glob` tool returns the ENTIRE tree when the worktree path contains the pattern's literal substring. Observed 2026-06-09 in live brodex session cccf6ea5 (task 6e6ae4be): agent called glob {pattern:"**/*fleet*", sort:"name"} and got back AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, Cargo.toml, crates/bbox-chunker/... — the full repo, none of which contain "fleet".

ROOT CAUSE (crates/bro-tools/src/workspace.rs Glob::call):
- :1239 GlobPattern::new(&args.pattern).compile_matcher() — globset's `Glob` defaults to literal_separator=FALSE, so `*` matches across `/`. Thus `**/*fleet*` degenerates to "any path containing 'fleet' anywhere".
- :1256 `if matcher.is_match(rel) || matcher.is_match(p)` — it also matches against `p`, the ABSOLUTE path. The session's worktree was `~/.local/state/blackbox/bro/fleet/worktrees/transcript-search/how-do-i-make-fleet-tui-update-set-a-17684737/...` — the prefix contains "fleet" in BOTH `/bro/fleet/` and the worktree dir name `how-do-i-make-fleet-tui-...`. So every file's absolute path matches `**/*fleet*` via the is_match(p) arm → whole tree returned. (is_match(rel) on "AGENTS.md" correctly does NOT match; the absolute-path arm is the leak.)

FIX SHAPE: (1) match ONLY against `rel` (the agent's pattern is worktree-relative); drop the `|| matcher.is_match(p)` absolute-path arm, or strip to the base-relative path before matching — the worktree prefix must never enter the match. (2) Consider GlobBuilder::literal_separator(true) so `*` doesn't span `/` and `**` is the only cross-dir token (standard glob semantics agents expect). Add a regression test: a glob run from a base dir whose absolute path contains the pattern substring must NOT match non-matching files. Note content_search's `glob:"*.rs"` filter worked in the same session (it happens to match basenames either way), so the bug bites recursive/substring patterns specifically.

Gap-worthy (tool primitive defect) — file a tool-surface gap if pursued; tracked here for now alongside the apply_patch + nudge items.

RESOLVED B1 + B3 — landed in commit 0589802 on beta/blackbox-v2 (2026-06-09). Pivoted to validating our base tools against the openai/codex reference (../codex, Apache-2.0) and lifting/adapting.

B1 [RESOLVED] apply_patch now exists. New vendored/adapted crate `crates/bro-apply-patch` (codex parser.rs + seek_sequence.rs verbatim; a Blackbox-authored synchronous std::fs apply layer ported from codex compute_replacements/apply_replacements, with worktree containment). Exposed as the `ApplyPatch` bro-tools builtin: freeform tool whose freeform_grammar() returns codex's apply_patch.lark; terse codex-style description (no prose block). DECISION (operator): brodex/Responses-ONLY via a general "grammar-transport rule" — TransportKind::honors_grammar() (Responses only); agent_loop drops any grammar-requiring builtin on non-grammar transports, so apply_patch never degrades to an unconstrained JSON-string editor competing with file_edit on Anthropic. Attribution: crates/bro-apply-patch/NOTICE + inline comments (matches bro-code-mode/NOTICE precedent). LIVE-VALIDATED both directions: brodex/Responses accepts the lark grammar and round-trips apply_patch end-to-end (files applied); glm/Anthropic never offers it (0 apply_patch tool_use, falls back to shell) even when explicitly instructed to use it. Unit: 14 apply-patch tests + tool test green.

B3 [RESOLVED] glob `**/*fleet*`-returns-everything bug fixed (crates/bro-tools/src/workspace.rs). Root cause was matching the matcher against the ABSOLUTE path whose worktree prefix contained "fleet". Now: match base-RELATIVE path only (dropped the `|| is_match(p)` arm), literal_separator(true) (cf. codex permissions::build_glob_matcher), + basename fallback so slash-less patterns (`*.rs`) stay recursive (fd/rg `-g` ergonomics). Regression test added; 4/4 glob tests green.
